clips.title: Using OIDC With HashiCorp Vault and GitHub Actions
clips.why: HashiCorp walks through the fields inside the token a GitHub job sends to Vault, the same claims the lab mints.
look: Which claim names the repo, which names the ref, and which names the workflow file.
That the token is signed by GitHub, so a job cannot change its own claims.
Think about which of these claims is the narrowest one to trust.
clips.after: Our gha-runners role used to trust the wide one, sub with a star; it now trusts job_workflow_ref with a list of files.

clips.title: Securely deploy to AWS with GitHub Actions and OIDC
clips.why: GitHub's own walkthrough of the same idea on AWS: a role that trusts GitHub's token only when its claims match.
look: The trust policy's condition on the token's claims, the AWS name for bound claims.
How a wildcard in that condition decides how many repos and branches can use the role.
That no secret is stored in GitHub at all; the signed token is the identity.
clips.after: Vault's bound_claims and AWS's trust conditions answer the same question, so the same rule applies: bind the narrowest claim you can.

clips.title: What Are AI Identities? Understanding Agentic Systems & Governance
clips.why: A clear whiteboard talk on why each AI agent needs an identity of its own, separate from the people who run it.
look: Why an agent should not borrow a person's identity.
How giving each agent its own identity makes access easy to limit and easy to remove.
Where he talks about knowing which agent did what: our meter per workload.
clips.after: Our agents act as one GitHub App and call Claude with one key per workload, so every action and every dollar points to one agent.

practice.q: Which claim names the exact workflow file a GitHub Actions job is running, so a reusable workflow matches whoever calls it?

options.why: That is only the repo. Every workflow in the repo would match.
sub holds the repo and the ref, not the file.
It holds the workflow file and its ref, such as RhinoHealth/fcp/.github/workflows/_cloud-int-tests-reusable-qa.yml@refs/heads/main.

practice.q: Finish the role so the patterns are wildcards, not exact text.
practice.hint: The other choice is string, which compares letter for letter.
practice.why: With glob, the star in _cloud-int-tests-reusable-*.yml@* matches every reusable file and every branch. With string, no real job would match.

practice.q: A DevOps admin stores a new Anthropic key. Which way keeps it out of the shell history and the process list?

options.why: The key is now in the shell history and visible to anyone who lists processes while it runs.

options.text: printf '%s' "$key" | vault kv patch -mount=kvv2 infrastructure/ai-agents/anthropic nova=-
options.why: =- tells Vault to read the value from stdin, and the key was read with read -s, so it is never on the command line.

options.text: Paste it into the ticket so DevOps can copy it into Vault later.
options.why: A key in a ticket is a key for everyone who can read Jira, forever.

practice.q: Put the safe rollout of the narrowed Vault role in order.
items: List every workflow that uses gha-runners today with a code search
Write the job_workflow_ref list in the role, leaving the admin policy unchanged
A person runs plan and apply over the VPN
Rerun one job per repo and confirm each still logs in
Confirm a job from any other repo is refused
Open the follow-up for least-privilege roles
practice.why: Find the real callers, change one thing, prove nobody legitimate lost access, prove the door is closed, then plan the next step.

practice.q: Why does the agents' Anthropic org stay separate from the org people use for Claude Code?

options.text: Because an org set up for HIPAA work and an org set up for zero data retention cannot be the same org.
options.why: The agents must run under ZDR, so they get their own org, with its own workspaces and keys.

options.text: Because agents are not allowed to use Opus 5.5.
options.why: Opus 5.5 is available under ZDR and is Nova's default model.

options.text: Because people's org cannot create API keys.
options.why: The reason is the data-retention setup, not a missing feature.
